note: The selected second output adds padding to every cell. The source PNG is copied intact; no color removal, pixelation filter, resampling or connected-component cropping was applied. Runtime cell bounds preserve all opaque pieces, including detached extremities.
localAdaptations: The shared catalog leaves several anatomies open. Grovefang is a local Groveflower host; Corpse Borer is a local giant-corpse specialist. Regional forms are local art variants, not new canonical rules. Bodies express the ecological briefs; advanced time, incubation and succession behavior is not implied by art alone.

steps.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: one production sprite atlas for an original overhead pixel-art RPG, The Hollow.
Create EXACTLY 64 separate full-body monster/animal sprites arranged in a STRICT REGULAR 8 COLUMNS x 8 ROWS grid on a square TRANSPARENT canvas. Exactly eight sprites in every row. All cells identical. No captions, text, cell borders, grid lines, scenery, ground tiles or decorative frame.
STYLE: charming strange creatures with native chunky 32x32 to 40x40 pixel designs, visually enlarged with crisp square pixel clusters. Dark 1-native-pixel outlines, 3 or 4 flat shades per material, small limited harmonious woodland palette. Classic 16-bit overhead RPG sprites with a consistent three-quarter overhead camera, visible tops and fronts, bodies facing southeast. Clear small silhouettes and readable animal faces; avoid realistic detail, tiny stippling, smooth painting, gradients or 3D rendering. No postprocessed blurry illustration. Like lovingly authored tiny pixel sprites.
FRAMING: Entire creature visible in each cell including head, feet, horns, tail and wings. Each body fits within the central 68% of its cell, with minimum16% transparent padding on ALL sides. Consistent ground baseline at82% cell height. Nothing touches a cell edge. Tall antlers and curling tails must stay within the padded cell. One complete figure per cell.

ROWS1-4 are32 distinct designs in this exact left-to-right order:
ROW1:
1 Grovefang: low slate-blue feline hunter with several peach flowers and green leaves rooted along its moving shoulders.
2 Overgrowth Stalker: crouching dark olive wolf-lizard, roots growing through skin and a heavy uneven fern mantle, visible face and four legs.
3 Pollen Hunter: pale tan long-eared mantis-cat with a broad protective green brow visor and amber double eyelids.
4 Cuphorn: stout small green-grey ungulate with two huge bowl-shaped curved horns holding water and reeds.
5 Sap Drinker: honey-brown squat lizard with striped warning neck, long curled red tongue and sticky amber sap on its chin.
6 Alarm Caller: upright ochre bird with a large flared red throat pouch, small wings and long toes.
7 Veilspinner: silver-lilac spider with translucent broad mist-catching fan membranes between eight legs, not a generic black spider.
8 Ridgeback Burrower: blunt-nosed brown mole-beast with turquoise porous stone ridges on its back and huge digging claws.
ROW2:
1 Burial Stag: weathered dark deer carrying small living green saplings and hanging roots in its branching antlers.
2 Uphill Carrier: stocky rusty goat-bear carrying a bundle of roots in its mouth, strong forequarters and moss on its back.
3 Scent Thief: small cream-and-russet long-tailed mammal with furry oversized cheek pouches, alert nose, low mischievous posture.
4 Rootknife Follower: little ragged mauve scavenger bird with a long thin beak, large yellow eyes and spindly legs.
5 Corpse Borer: big ivory-and-rust plated beetle with shovel mandibles and cream fungal nodules on its shell.
6 Velvet Anchor: round charcoal tortoise with a deep velvety teal moss garden growing on its rounded rock shell, tiny pale head.
7 Eggrunner: slender tawny six-legged ferret with broad silver temporal whiskers, one striped egg cradled in its forepaws.
8 Gradient Broodling: threatening purple-black young predatory reptile with long scythe forelimbs, ivory facial mask and fragments of a violet-banded eggshell at its tail.
ROW3:
1 Tapping Hunter: pale icy-blue long-legged insect-fox with long black tapping forelimbs and pointed triangular ears.
2 Snowbell Grazer: round white woolly small yak with wide listening ears and two blue shovel tusks, snowbell flowers tucked in its fur.
3 Cache Finder: little dark blue-grey arctic mustelid with an ivory muzzle and bushy white-tipped tail, carrying a frozen bone.
4 Cold Garden Grazer: broad shaggy cream muskox with miniature cyan fungi and frost-covered red berries growing in its long fur.
5 Stillglass: small translucent jade crystalline crab with six fan-shaped filter limbs and gold debris inside its glass body.
6 Threshold Heron: elegant lilac-and-white heron, one leg raised, a dark blue crescent crest and warm yellow long beak.
7 Duskcoil: coiled indigo serpent with copper scale rings, blunt leaf-shaped head and pale featherlike neck frill.
8 Glassbrood: obsidian-and-turquoise salamander with swollen translucent amber egg sacs along its back, glowing mineral spots.
ROW4: regional variants of existing Hollow animals, clearly distinct from their ordinary versions:
1 pale bark-armored Barkjaw, six short spider-mouth limbs, mossy cream plates and tiny russet horns;
2 Rootknife with pale birch-striped long green lizard body and hooked mantis forelegs;
3 Mantleback tortoise with a broad cluster of lilac shelf mushrooms instead of orange ones;
4 Rime Antler deer with dark grey winter coat, wide ice antlers and reddish hanging antler gardens;
5 Snowkeel broad pale snow-swimming beast with a split dorsal blue fin and short digging paddles;
6 Ventback basalt-armored lizard with three squat copper-red smoking dorsal chimneys;
7 Boundary Scavenger with rusty banded long tail, six legs, one blue throat sac and one amber throat sac;
8 cream-and-lilac Petalmaw orchid monster on dark root feet, pale toothed flower-face.

ROWS5-8 repeat EXACTLY the designs in ROWS1-4 respectively, same order, same scale and silhouettes, with one SMALL second animation pose: a step forward, shifted feet, a slight head turn, opening wings or a feeding posture. These are ANIMATION PAIRS of the first32, not new unrelated species. Keep all markings, clothing-free animal anatomy and colors consistent between pairs. Row5 is row1 walking; row6 is row2 walking; row7 is row3 walking; row8 is row4 walking.
Strict64-cell atlas, transparent outside sprites, full bodies preserved, chunky pixel artwork and exact 8x8 alignment take priority over fine detail.

Edit this sprite atlas with one targeted layout correction. Preserve exactly the same64 creatures, colors, chunky pixel-art style and pairing order. Keep EXACTLY8 columns and8 rows with equal cells, transparent background. Reduce EACH individual creature to72% of its current dimensions around the center of its own cell, so every head, horn, tail, foot and wing sits comfortably inside its cell, with at least15% transparent padding on every side. Do not scale the whole atlas as one image; independently shrink the contents of every cell while keeping the cells the same size and grid in the same position. All complete bodies must remain visible. If a horn, reed, tail or foot previously touched a cell boundary, complete its contour naturally. Final baseline at82% of each cell height. No sprite may cross or touch a cell boundary. No new objects, no scenery, no labels, no grid lines. Preserve the transparent canvas, pixel edges and recognizable anatomy. Priority: clean isolated full silhouettes with comfortable padding in a strict8x8 grid.
